title: Company entitlement record — the decoded JWS payload of /entitlements/{co_ulid}.jws
description:
The signed, scanner-facing proof that an organisation holds coverage. Served unauthenticated as a compact ES256 JWS with `Content-Type: application/jose` (FS10-060, WEB-096); THIS schema describes the DECODED PAYLOAD, not the compact serialisation. The signing key is born non-exportable in the movement's own Key Vault and the `kid` sits in the JWS header (FS-00 §6.4). A consumer MUST verify the signature against the published JWKS before trusting anything here — the coverage function treats a record that fails verification as `no` (FS-10 §4.2). At P-M2 this record IS the coverage proof: there is no coverage route at v0 (FS-00 §6.10 as amended), and the record doubles as the vesting snapshot (VS-33/COM-015).

RATIFIED (FS-00 §6.2 amendment note of 2026-09-07; history in the CHANGELOG's Settled list): the payload is this COMPANY record. The FS-00 §6.2 amendment note of 2026-09-01 had stated it as the single entitlement object `{entId, lane, scope, status, periodStart, periodEnd, graceEnd?, scheduleVersion, vestedWindows[], thresholdRegistration?}`, while FS-10 §4.2 (the consumer contract, and the only place that specifies `domains[]`/`verification`/domain resolution) stated it as a COMPANY record carrying `entitlements[]` of exactly that object; the 2026-09-07 note ratifies the company record and leaves the frozen object untouched inside the array, closed to additions. Both texts are then satisfied — the frozen object is unchanged, it simply appears in the array. This file was written to FS-10 §4.2 from the start and does not change: no property moved, no version was bumped. One organisation, one record, one URL, however many terms it holds.

Published `status` is a PROJECTION of the internal state machine onto `active | suspended | void` (FS05-052): `pending` is never published, `revoked` publishes as `void`, and grace/lapse are NEVER published statuses — cov-v1 derives them from the dates (`now ≤ periodEnd` → active window; `periodEnd < now ≤ graceEnd` → lapsed-in-grace; beyond `graceEnd` → no contribution).

VESTING (D12 as amended, 5th collision): each element of `vestedWindows[]` records one paid term `{from, to}` and the test is `version publication date ≤ to` — the back catalogue at activation vests together with everything published during the term. `from` is term provenance and never a lower bound on vesting.

generatedAt.description: When this record was signed and published. Republished on every purchase, renewal, lapse, suspension or void (FS-00 §6.2).

coId.description: Platform company ULID — the only company reference that may appear in a shareable, CDN-cached, log-visible GET URL (WEB-143).

name.description: Legal name. OPTIONAL and OPT-IN: directory naming defaults to unnamed, and the browsable supporter directory lists only opted-in payers. An opted-out payer's record still verifies at its own URL — the proof does not depend on being named (VS-33).

domains.description: Domains associated with this organisation. Domain-keyed coverage lookups resolve ONLY through domain-verified entries (the `/entitlements/domain-index.json` artifact, FS10-024) and only over POST — a third-party organisation identifier never appears in a GET URL (WEB-143).

verification.description: Company verification state (FS-00 §6.1). A waiver grant mints an `unverified` stub so a waived organisation with no account still resolves by ULID (FS-10 §4.3 step 2).

entitlements.description: Every term this organisation holds, current and past. An empty array is valid: a waiver-grant stub has no entitlement at all, and its coverage comes from the waiver registry.

thresholdRegistration.description: Record-level self-certification that the organisation is under the licence's revenue/size threshold (COM-054…060). Travels inside this same signed record, which is why the under-threshold answer still carries an entitlement-JWS proof (FS-10 §4.4). Not operable at P-M2 (P-M2 §5 item 13): the licence's threshold test is self-executing, so under-threshold organisations need no registration to be covered.

entitlement.description: The FROZEN entitlement object (FS-00 §6.2 amendment note 2026-09-01; producer FS-05). Closed to additions: a new field requires an FS-00 amendment, and a new meaning requires a new schema version.

lane.description: Commercial lane. cov-v1 evaluates lanes in the COM-009 enumeration order: pass, then project, then portfolio (donation is answered after waivers). At P-M2 only `project` is purchasable — Pass and Portfolio are published schedule with honest 'not yet purchasable' copy (VS-14).

status.description: The PUBLISHED projection (FS05-052). `suspended` = chargeback notice stage 1, and answers `no` immediately (COM-024). `void` = refunded or upheld chargeback, void ab initio. `pending` is never published; `grace` and `lapsed` are never published — they are derived from the dates.

periodEnd.description: End of the paid term. `now == periodEnd` is still INSIDE the term (FS10-121 boundary rule).

graceEnd.description: periodEnd + 30 days (COM-042). `periodEnd < now ≤ graceEnd` derives `lapsed-in-grace`; `now == graceEnd` is still grace; beyond it the term contributes nothing. Absent means no grace window is published for this term.

scheduleVersion.description: The fee-schedule version this term was priced under. Renewals price at the then-current version (COM-041); nothing is ever repriced retroactively (D12).

vestedWindows.description: One element per paid, settled, unreversed term. Vesting test: a covered version is vested permanently iff its publication date ≤ a window's `to`. Monotonically non-decreasing except the payment-reversal void (FS05-062).

from.description: Term start — provenance only. NEVER a lower bound on vesting: the back catalogue at activation is vested too (D12 as amended, 5th collision).

to.description: Term end — the operative bound. Every covered version published on or before this date is vested permanently.

thresholdRegistration.description: Per-term threshold self-certification, when it was recorded against a term rather than the organisation. cov-v1 reads the record-level block first, then any entitlement-level block, taking the latest `expiresAt`.

scope.description: Structured scope. `project` ⇒ `repos[]` (min 1, cap 50 declared repositories, COM-018); `portfolio` ⇒ `org`; `network` (Pass) ⇒ neither — a Pass covers every registered repository, which is why it wins the precedence order.

org.description: Owner-organisation node_id, compared against the repo record's `owner.orgId` (FS-10 §4.3 step 5c).

selfCertifiedAt.description: One tick, no audit (D8). Echoed in the coverage answer's `dates` block.

expiresAt.description: After this instant the registration falls through and coverage reverts toward `no` (COM-055/057).

githubNodeId.description: A GitHub GraphQL node_id, in either of the two forms GitHub has issued: the opaque current form (a repository's is `R_`-prefixed) and the legacy base64 form, whose decoded value begins `010:Repository` and whose `=` padding the first alternative cannot express. Widened 2026-09-08 to admit the second: `registry-v0-record.v1` accepts both, so a record the curated registry accepts is publishable in this artifact. The primary key for repositories and people throughout this contract set (FS-00 §6.1).
